claims.text: Tribological loading forms an adaptive near-surface tribofilm or nanostructured layer in high-entropy-alloy coatings.
The adaptive near-surface layer is the primary factor governing the low wear rate of high-entropy-alloy coatings.
A multielement lattice promotes in-situ chemical reactions and severe plastic deformation during sliding.
Sliding-induced reactions and severe plastic deformation produce a protective, dynamically evolving tribofilm and refine near-surface grains.
The tribofilm and refined near-surface grains reduce friction and material removal.
The initial AlCoCrFeNi coating is magnetron-sputtered, has uniform equiaxed grains, and has no pre-existing surface film.
Adding Mo is expected to stabilize tribofilm formation relative to an otherwise identical undoped coating.
The relevant mediator is an emergent tribofilm or heavily refined near-surface nanocrystalline layer generated by frictional contact.
Multicomponent synergy promotes local dynamic reactions and structural rearrangements that build a self-lubricating film or nanostructured region.
The self-lubricating film or nanostructured region limits plowing and crack initiation.
A dopant that facilitates tribofilm nucleation or reaction will reduce friction and wear relative to the undoped control.
Coatings unable to form robust tribofilms will have higher wear rates and friction coefficients.
Undoped coatings or coatings tested under conditions that preclude tribofilm formation will exhibit higher wear and friction than doped or tribofilm-optimized variants.
The proposed effect should hold only below loads that compromise coating integrity.
The proposed effect should hold at temperatures up to approximately 500–600 °C, provided the coating does not melt or its phases do not destabilize.
It remains unresolved whether tribofilm chemistry or the subsurface nanocrystalline structure is the primary contributor to wear mitigation.
Similar tribological performance despite measurably different tribofilm formation would falsify the proposed governing role of the tribofilm.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis allows either a tribofilm or a refined subsurface nanocrystalline layer to govern wear, and the uncertainty field states that the subsurface structure may be primary. Nevertheless, the falsification rule treats failure to form a distinct protective surface layer as sufficient to invalidate the hypothesis, without requiring absence of the alternative nanostructured mediator.
